children: Shares of Pace Digitek Ltd jumped nearly 13 per cent in morning trade on Tuesday after the company announced that its material subsidiary had secured an order worth Rs 488.46 crore from an NTPC unit.
The stock climbed 13.11 per cent to Rs 175.37 per share on the NSE. It later pared some gains and was trading 9.98 per cent higher at Rs 170.31 at around 11:50 am.

The sharp uptick came after Pace Digitek said in an exchange filing that its material subsidiary, Lineage Power Pvt Ltd (LPPL), had secured an order valued at Rs 4,884.6 million, including GST, from NTPC GE Power Services Pvt Ltd (NGSL) for the Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) project at Barh STPP (NTPC Stages I & II).
The order covers the supply, testing, supervision of erection and commissioning of BESS containers, along with Battery Management Systems (BMS) and Energy Management Systems (EMS).
It also includes five years of annual maintenance services and a further seven-year extended warranty for the battery containers.
The order is scheduled to be completed by December 31, 2026.
According to the company, LPPL is being developed as a product-led BESS business covering manufacturing, product supply, system integration and lifecycle support.
Pace Digitek said it operationalised 2.5 GWh of BESS manufacturing capacity in 2025, expanded it to 5 GWh and plans to scale the capacity to 10 GWh by the third quarter of FY2027.
The company has delivered BESS containers representing more than 1.5 GWh of capacity so far.
The company said it also sees commercial and industrial applications as an emerging opportunity alongside its utility-scale BESS business.
Pace Digitek Chairman and Managing Director Venugopalrao Maddisetty said the order was an important step in strengthening LPPL as a product-led BESS business.

"It brings together product supply, commissioning and long-term lifecycle support, enabling us to deepen our participation across the BESS value chain and strengthen our engagement with customers beyond manufacturing," he said.
The company said it would continue to invest in capabilities to support customers across the lifecycle of energy-storage systems.
